axes.name: Original obligations and negative constraints
axes.assessment: C1–C6 are all addressed, and each negative constraint is maintained as a proposed boundary. C1 identity, C2 ordinary cancel/move and existing-override handling, C4 provider comparison, C5 loss-aware/idempotent import, and C6 honest validation/unsupported status are substantive. C3’s asserted generated-gap policy is materially wrong; structural clause coverage does not qualify its source meaning.

axes.name: Consequential claims, exact subject/operation/version/default/unit/type/domain/exceptions
axes.assessment: The 19-claim independent map distinguishes RFC file semantics, provider operation contracts, public package documentation, and unexecuted design choices. Most subject/type/default/condition claims are supported. F01 survives in the final: original RFC §3.3.10 is internally contradictory and Verified4271 resolves the generated-time condition. Minor carried aimcal release metadata and Graph retrieval locators are separately bounded.

axes.name: Useful unfamiliar discovery, alternatives, implementation/history and opportunity breadth
axes.assessment: Discovery is substantive, not vacuous caution: detached-original-slot editing, EXDATE precedence/DTSTART retention, Google immutable originalStartTime, Graph UTC originalStart and adjacent-day limits, parser-versus-validator distinction, retained-property model, recurrence candidate limits, and source-scoped upsert are useful. It compares Google and Graph operations, component/raw-property retention approaches, ical-rs versus aimcal-ical, and rrule2 rather than installing a library without qualification. Archive history is relevant. The consequential standards-history investigation missed Verified4271, already available since2015, which undermines the DST/dependency judgment. No unrelated provider/service breadth is demanded.

axes.name: Wrong criticism, corrections, rejections and every exact plan disposition
axes.assessment: Critic1’s request for a deterministic weekly subset is useful without making optional RFC parts mandatory; final explicitly chooses a narrower valid subset. Critic2’s explicit type/local-form validation is supported; matching TZID is a product profile restriction. Critic3 is materially wrong in current governing context and final accepts it. The original user’s new-UID/current-start/authoritative-UTC-row hypotheses are correctly rejected or amended. The additional VALUE/property explanation is correct, with limited retrospective defect attribution.

axes.name: Supported discovery/draft/critique/final meaning preserved
axes.assessment: Master/original-slot identity, local zone data, ordinary cancellation, exception movement, narrow scope, loss-aware retention, source-scoped upsert, provider boundaries, alternatives, and honest validation status survive all stages. The final adds an explicit profile and type checks instead of replacing substance with predecessor IDs. The investigator’s general rrule2 gap-documentation characterization was not disproved by the corrected standard; the critic falsely recasts it as a divergence and the final repeats that rejection. The investigator’s own separate skip-policy text was already wrong and remains. These are traced separately, without pretending the final repaired them.

axes.name: Meaningful proposed versus executed validation and oracle applicability
axes.assessment: The matrix gives observable identity, offset, component/payload, cardinality and no-mutation invariants. All seven original proposed cases remain; actual execution is consistently none. Local round-trip is correctly separated from provider interoperability. However the additional generated-gap row uses the erroneous skip/noncount oracle and can approve the wrong policy or reject a documented erratum-aligned engine. An ordinary18:30 clock-change fixture is not a gap-policy discriminator. Hash checks and documentation reads are not product validation.

material_findings.classification: material wrong / unsupported consequential correction and validation oracle
material_findings.root_cause: RFC 5545 §3.3.10 read selectively without its later conflicting passage or Verified technical erratum4271
material_findings.summary: The final mandates ignoring/not counting a generated nonexistent local time as the governing RFC policy and accepts the critic’s claim that rrule2 generated pre-gap-offset behavior is nonconformant. Verified4271 instead directs generated nonexistent local times to §3.3.5; invalid dates still are ignored. The purported library divergence and the skip-based prospective oracle are unsupported.

primary_evidence.locator: Verified technical erratum 4271 and corrected text

material_findings.materiality: The first-release profile does not exclude weekly local start times that fall in spring gaps; C3 expressly asks for nonexistent-time policy. The recommendation changes which occurrence exists, its instant, a dependency qualification decision, and a discriminating future test oracle. An ordinary18:30 fixture may not encounter a gap, but cannot make the general policy/rejection correct.
material_findings.scope_boundary: This is a planning/source/critique defect, not an executed importer defect or a claim of actual lost bookings. A custom skip policy could be chosen explicitly; the frozen final instead represents it as RFC-mandated and rejects the documented alternative as divergent.
